parameters.content:
## Audit Notion wiki health for orphan, stale and thin pages

Runs a weekly rule-based sweep of a Notion wiki, builds the internal link graph from page content, and flags pages that nobody links to, nobody has edited, or nobody has written. Findings land in a Notion database and a ranked digest goes to Slack. No AI is involved, every classification is a threshold you set.

### How it works

1. A weekly schedule fires and one Set node supplies the wiki search text, the `Wiki Health` database, the Slack channel and every threshold.
2. Notion page search returns every page the integration can read, with `simple` off so `last_edited_time` survives.
3. The workflow loops one page at a time and pulls all blocks recursively with `simplifyOutput` off, so page mentions keep their target ids.
4. A Code node counts words and collects outbound links from mentions, `link_to_page` blocks, child pages and pasted notion.so URLs.
5. A second Code node inverts those edges into inbound counts, then labels each page orphan, stale, thin or healthy and adds a weighted score.
6. Flagged pages are matched against existing `Wiki Health` rows, written back as an update or a create, and the ranked digest posts to Slack.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect a Notion internal integration credential and share only the wiki root page with it, so page search returns the wiki and nothing else.
- [ ] Connect a Slack credential with `chat:write` and invite the bot to the digest channel.
- [ ] Create a `Wiki Health` database with `Page` (title), `Page ID` (rich text), `Status` (rich text), `Score` (number), `Word Count` (number), `Inbound Links` (number), `Broken Links` (number), `Page URL` (url) and `Last Audited` (date).
- [ ] Open `Set Wiki Audit Config` and fill in the wiki search text, the `Wiki Health` database ID and the Slack channel ID.
- [ ] The Notion API allows about three requests per second, so a 200 to 400 page wiki finishes comfortably. Point the integration at a narrower root above that size.

### Customization

`staleAfterDays`, `thinWordCount` and `digestSize` set the thresholds. `orphanWeight`, `staleWeight`, `thinWeight` and `brokenLinkWeight` decide how the digest ranks, so raise `orphanWeight` if unlinked pages matter most to your team.

## Weekly schedule and config

Fires every Monday morning. `Set Wiki Audit Config` holds the only user-specific values, the wiki search text, the `Wiki Health` database ID, the Slack channel and all thresholds.

## Crawl pages and blocks

Page search runs with `simple` off so `last_edited_time` comes back. The loop pulls blocks one page at a time with `fetchNestedBlocks` on and `simplifyOutput` off, then counts words and collects link targets. Empty pages still emit an item so the loop keeps moving.

## Score every page

Inverts outbound links into inbound counts, then labels each page orphan, stale, thin or healthy. The weighted score decides digest order.

A page the integration could not read is flagged Fetch failed and skips the orphan and thin checks, so a permissions problem does not read as a content problem.

## Rank and post the digest

Runs once on the whole result set. Sorts flagged pages by score, keeps the top `digestSize`, and posts one Slack message with the totals above the list.

## Match findings to existing rows

Notion has no upsert. The database is queried once, findings are matched on the `Page ID` property, and the branch decides between update and create.

## Write rows back to Notion

Update keeps the existing row and refreshes `Status`, `Score` and the counts. Create adds `Page ID` and `Page URL` as well, so the next run can match it.

## Two settings that silently break this

`Get Page Blocks From Notion` must keep `simplifyOutput` off. Simplified output flattens rich text into a plain string and drops the mention page ids, so the link graph empties and every page reads as an orphan.

`Search Wiki Pages In Notion` must keep `simple` off. Simplified output returns only id, name and url, with no `last_edited_time`, so nothing is ever stale.
